summary: The US-Iran standoff remains the dominant force, with the 10-year yield rising to 4.62% as Iran's Supreme Leader hardened Tehran's position on uranium enrichment, stoking fresh oil supply and inflation fears. Reinforcing the pressure, FOMC minutes revealed most policymakers see additional rate hikes as warranted if inflation stays above target — keeping real rates elevated, weighing on gold and bonds while equities hold their risk-on posture.
tweet: Iran peace talks stall and FOMC minutes flag more hikes — the 10Y hit 4.62%, squeezing gold and bonds while stocks shrug it off.
